tasks.title: Close out 12 orders open more than 60 days ($1,470)
tasks.why: 12 orders worth $1,470 have been open longer than 60 days, out of 31 open orders worth $4,715 in total. The oldest is osmanbey_35 at 277 days. Every one of these buyers has already paid or committed, so this is not new business to win — it is delivered-or-owed work nobody closed. steps: Open each order and establish one thing: is the client waiting on us, are we waiting on the client, or is it dead. That answer decides everything else and takes a minute per order.
Where we owe work — assign it to the designer named on the row with a delivery date this week. Oldest first: osmanbey_35 (277d, $250), jordyspikker (149d, $100), calumsnell (147d, $100).

Where it is genuinely dead — set the status so it stops appearing here, and note why in the CSR column.
Anything still open at this time next week gets escalated, not re-listed.

tasks.title: Organic decline is a ranking problem — act accordingly
tasks.why: Orders moved -6.5% over 14 days (200 -> 187). 52% of that swing is reach, which fell: impressions 252,223 -> 96,474, CTR 1.51% -> 1.56%, close rate 5.2% -> 12.5%. That makes this a ranking problem — work on review velocity, on-time delivery, response time.

tasks.why: Dulal Khan averages $124 across 9 orders; Nimeazad averages $78 across 17. Some of that is brief mix rather than skill — but routing the $200+ briefs to the designers who already deliver at that level protects both AOV and rating.
steps: Assign every brief above $200 to Dulal Khan or the next two by AOV.
Check whether the low-AOV designers are getting low-value briefs or producing low-value outcomes before acting on this.
Revisit in 30 days with the engine's updated per-designer AOV.

tasks.title: Follow up the 5 quotes that never got one ($527)
tasks.why: 5 buyers were quoted $527 between them and no follow-up was ever logged against any of them — the largest is akhilkpfxx at $160, quoted 158 days ago. That sits inside a total unanswered pipeline of $6,232 across 21 leads. Of the 25 quoted leads anyone did chase, 9 placed (36%); this is costed at half that, because these are older. Note the raw split is misleading: quoted leads with no follow-up appear to convert at 93%, but that is because a follow-up only gets logged when the buyer did not say yes immediately. These 5 are the residue of that group, not part of its success.
steps: Work the never-followed-up list first, largest first: akhilkpfxx ($160, 158d), architpatel497 ($147, 46d), kai_utzinger ($85, 105d), zain_qw ($75, 40d).
One message each. State the quote is still open, and ask one question they can answer in a word — whether the project is still live. Do not re-pitch and do not discount unprompted.
Log the touch in the FollowUp column the same day, or the next run will tell you to send it again.
Then work the remainder by value; treat a third unanswered follow-up as a no and stop.

tasks.title: Start recording upsells — the column is empty
tasks.why: Upsell is marked on 0.0% of the 125 orders whose tab has an Upsell column. That is not a low upsell rate, it is an unused column. The highest-value lever in the funnel currently cannot be measured, which means it cannot be improved or defended.
steps: Fill the Upsell column on every order: TRUE/FALSE, no blanks.
Fill 'What did you upsell and how much' whenever TRUE.
Backfill the last 30 completed orders from memory this week.

Never move a pre-order conversation off Fiverr, and never argue.

edge.title: Dygram is the experiment already run
edge.detail: Dygram holds Success Score 9 against X Studioz's 8, and pulls 8x the impressions (12,700/day against 1,564). Same operator, same team, same category, same marketplace. Whatever is different between the two profiles is worth more than any competitor study — diagnose it directly rather than theorising about the algorithm.

edge.title: 1,583 reviews is the moat, and it is being spent on cheap orders
edge.detail: Almost no competitor in logo design can match that review base. It is a conversion advantage that compounds — and it is currently attached to a low average order value. The same trust aimed at $150-$260 work is the single largest untaken edge here, and it costs nothing to try.

edge.title: Half the revenue is from people who already know you
edge.detail: 158 of 574 clients have ordered more than once, producing 48.2% of orders and $38,724 of revenue — with the Upsell column at 0.0% filled. Competitors fight for the first order. Nobody is fighting for the second one here, including us.
